home.title: Spindro: free, open-source indoor cycling app for smart trainers
home.description: Free, open-source indoor cycling app. ERG and virtual gears for your smart trainer, structured workouts and six games that are workouts. No subscription, no account. Browser and Android.

faq.a: Yes. No subscription, no ads, no in-app purchases. The source code is open on GitHub. The project is run by one person; you can help with bug reports, trainer reports and code.
No. You open the app and ride. Your rides, records and settings stay on your device. You can export a backup to move them to another device.

faq.q: Does it work on iPhone and iPad?
faq.a: Not in Safari: Apple does not allow Web Bluetooth there. A browser that adds Web Bluetooth, such as Bluefy, should work; we have not tested it. A native iOS app may come later.

faq.q: Which browser and device do I need?
faq.a: Android: Chrome, or the Android app. PC, Mac, Linux and ChromeOS: Chrome or Edge with Bluetooth. The page must be served over HTTPS. The web app can also be installed from the browser menu, and it offers to reload when a new version is ready. The screen stays on while you ride.

Spindro speaks FTMS, the standard Bluetooth protocol used by most recent smart trainers. We have ridden one trainer for real. The compatibility page says what is verified, what should work, and how to report yours.

It does the trainer side: ERG, virtual gears, structured workouts and games. It is not an online virtual world: there is no multiplayer. A trainer accepts one Bluetooth connection at a time, so close other apps first.

faq.q: Can I write my own game?
faq.a: Yes. The games share a kit and a set of design rules. Start from the Build a game page.

faq.q: What happens to my data and privacy?
faq.a: This website has no cookies and no ads, and its fonts are served from the same site. We count visits anonymously with GoatCounter, with no cookies and no personal data. In the app, ride data stays on your device, and anonymous usage counting only starts if you agree. Data leaves the device only if you use Strava (it sends the ride to Strava), play a YouTube video (Google's player loads) or export a file. Read the privacy policy for the details.

home.kicker: Indoor cycling app · free and open source
home.lead: Spindro connects to your smart trainer over Bluetooth. Start a ride in ERG, follow a structured workout, or play games that run on your real watts. It works in the browser and on Android, with no account.
home.heroNote: Android: Chrome or the app. PC and Mac: Chrome or Edge. iPhone: the Bluefy browser.
home.heroAlt: The Spindro home screen with a trainer connected: a free ride in ERG with a 130 W target and a Start button, and shortcuts to workouts, games and history.

stages.title: Add a device, then ride
stages.text: The home is built around ERG: a Today card with a target in watts, − and + to change it, and one big Start button. One “Add device” button pairs a trainer, a Zwift controller, a heart rate strap, a power meter or a cadence sensor, and the app works out what each one is for, then suggests the next one. Known devices reconnect by themselves.
stages.alt: The Devices sheet listing a connected Van Rysel D100 trainer and a heart-rate strap, each with a Disconnect button, and the Add another device button.
rows: FTMS first; Tacx FE-C and Wahoo legacy as fallbacks
Zwift Click, Play and Ride as shifters and remote
Shows which key the app receives and lets you map it
The ride keeps recording and the app retries; a banner says which device dropped
Feel that the trainer obeys before you start

stages.title: Train with a plan
stages.text: Structured workouts and multi-week plans, scaled to your FTP. If you do not know it, a ramp test estimates it. While a workout runs, the cockpit shows the current step, the time left and the next one.
stages.alt: A workout in progress: 196 watts, a Sweet spot 3×10 workout in its warm-up with the step profile and the next step.

stages.title: Games that are workouts
stages.text: Six 3D games, each one a structured workout as a percentage of your FTP: 5, 10 or 20 minutes, three levels, efforts and recoveries, something to do every few seconds. They share one menu, so you learn it once.

stages.title: Your watch keeps the ride
stages.text: On Android the phone can broadcast power, cadence and speed as a Bluetooth sensor, so your watch records the ride and syncs it the way it always does. The app also keeps its own history.
stages.alt: Ride summary with time, distance, average power, kilojoules and power records.
rows: Garmin and others should work, not yet verified
.fit with the GPS track of a loaded route

games: A runner shooter. Shields break only at the right watts; a sprint unleashes overdrive.
Hold the road against waves of zombies on three lanes: switch lane to the nearest threat, ride through portals, level up your weapon with every effort.
Bridge to the riders who attack and tow them into your slipstream.
A timed stage: breakaway, intermediate sprint, climb and final sprint. Climbs load your trainer.
A pedal-powered plane: your watts are your altitude. Fly the rings that draw your workout.
Bounce a bottle off the soigneurs. Cadence sets its speed, watts charge the turbo.
home.gamesMore: The games menu also plays any YouTube ride video, or a video of your own, at your own speed. If the trainer drops during a game, the game pauses with a message.
gamesAlt: Pedal Strike: a rider on a harbour road facing a shielded mini-boss, with the score, the workout step bar and the overdrive meter.

Horde Run: a rider on a three-lane dusk road with zombies walking down the lanes, a lit strip showing the firing lane, a portal pair with plates above them (+1 ally, fire rate), the wave counter and six hearts.
Slipstream: a rider on a tree-lined road with a bar telling you to get in the next rider's lane, a countdown, and the wave and caught counters.
Breakaway: the rider in pink leads the bunch towards the sea, with the gear, the climb goal and a profile of the stage on screen.
Updraft: a yellow plane carrying the rider through a ring, with an altitude gauge.
Feed Zone: a rider bouncing a bottle off a line of fans holding buckets.
ownPoints: No subscription, no ads, no in-app purchases.
No account. Your rides stay on your device.
AGPL-3.0: the code is public and stays public.
Five languages. Works offline once loaded.

compat.title: Compatible trainers and watches | Spindro
compat.description: Smart trainers, Zwift controllers and watches that work with Spindro, and how sure we are: ridden for real, should work, reported by users. Only one trainer has been tested on real hardware.
compat.lead: Spindro picks the protocol on its own: FTMS, then Tacx FE-C over Bluetooth, then Wahoo legacy, then read-only Cycling Power or Speed & Cadence. Below is what we support and how sure we are.

statusDesc.verified: Tested on the real device by the author.
statusDesc.expected: The protocol is supported by the code, but this model has never been tried.
statusDesc.reported: Users told us it works. No report has been collected yet.
statusDesc.partial: Some functions were tested on the real device; the rest was not.

compat.reportText: Tried a trainer or watch? In the app, use “Report a problem”, or open an issue on GitHub with the model, what worked and what did not. Reports turn “should work” into “reported by users”.
compat.note: Tacx FE-C and Wahoo legacy support have been tested only against a simulated trainer. A trainer that accepts only one Bluetooth connection cannot be used by Spindro and another app at the same time.
compat.connectLead: Spindro needs Web Bluetooth, or the Android app. What works where:
connect: Bluetooth is built in. Android asks once for “Nearby devices”; known devices reconnect by themselves.
Web Bluetooth. Bluetooth on, and the “Nearby devices” permission for the browser.
Chrome, Edge or Opera on Windows, macOS, Linux, ChromeOS
Web Bluetooth. The page must be served over HTTPS.
No Web Bluetooth, and there is no Spindro app for iOS. A browser that adds it, such as Bluefy, should work; we have not tried it.
No Web Bluetooth. Use Chrome or Edge.
compat.connectNote: The connection flow (suggesting the next device, reconnecting, dropouts, “Test resistance”) has been exercised with simulated Bluetooth devices only.
compat.connectLink: Read the connection guide on GitHub

dev.title: Build a game for Spindro | Spindro
dev.description: Add a game to Spindro in about 15 minutes: copy the template, add one registry entry, add your strings, check it with the bot. Open source, plain JavaScript, no build step.
dev.lead: A Spindro game is one folder, one registry entry and its text strings. The repository has a template game, a guide that goes from a fresh clone to a game on your screen in about 15 minutes, an API reference, design rules, and a bot that checks your game.
dev.tempoAlt: The Tempo template game's start menu: a title, length and level buttons, how to play, and a Start button.
dev.tempoCaption: The template game, Tempo, in its start menu. The menu, the stars and the results screen come from the shared kit: you do not write them.
three: Copy the template folder: the template game is js/games/template/tempo.js, copied to js/games/<your id>/index.js, with its name and id replaced.
Add one entry to the registry in js/games/registry.js. While the game is not ready, mark it dev so it only shows in developer mode.
Add your strings (name, desc, help) in the five files locales/en, it, fr, es and de.json, and run the i18n check.
dev.pathText: You need Node 22 and git. There is no build step. This is the start of the guide:
dev.pathAfter: The demo flag replaces the trainer with a simulated rider with sliders for power and cadence, so you can play without a trainer. Reload the page after each change.
kit: hooks.stats() returns power, cadence, gear and heart rate; hooks.ftp() returns the FTP. Targets are fractions of FTP, never fixed watts.
One start menu (length, level) and one results screen for every game: long-press + or pedal to start, then stars and personal bests.
If hooks.workout() returns a plan, the workout decides the targets and the length.
Text and panel helpers in the kit's hud.js for readable on-screen numbers.
input(dir) receives exactly +1 or −1, from a Zwift Click or the keyboard. Every game must be playable with + / − and the pedals alone.
A three.js starter, js/games/template/skeleton3d.js, with the shared stage, sky, lights and cyclist.
dev.checkText: The check plays your game at 0.6, 0.8, 1.0 and 1.2 times FTP with the demo rider. It prints the stars earned, the time to the first event, the longest gap without an event, events per minute and milliseconds per frame, and when a rule is broken it says which one and how to fix it.
rules: A run is a workout of 5, 10 or 20 minutes, with intensity as a percentage of the rider's FTP, so it is fair at 120 W and at 320 W.
Three levels (easy, normal, hard) of your choosing; the targets stay exactly those of the plan.
Something to do within eight seconds, and never more than five seconds without an event that asks or rewards something.
Playable without touching the screen: watts and cadence do the work, + and − do one thing.
Whoever stops pedalling pauses the game; nobody is punished for pushing harder.
ship: Add the files your game imports to the ASSETS list in sw.js and bump the cache name.
Assets need a clear licence (CC0, MIT, OFL, or made for the project) and a credit in the README and the licences page.
A genre or a mechanic is fine; a clone of an existing commercial game is not.
Open a pull request against the beta branch, with the checklist from the design rules and the bot's table.
